brief:
Collective Website Clone & Reference Research — Codex Task Pack
Prepared: 2026-09-28
Codex kickoff prompt
Work through the projects below as separate brands and product surfaces. Start with an inventory and implementation plan. Do not edit code, overwrite an existing project, push commits, publish, or transmit this pack to a different Codex session before the user reviews the plan.
Stage 1 — inspect and plan
1. Read this entire pack and inspect each supplied reference, existing local project, and source repository where accessible.
2. For each project, report the route inventory, page-template families, unique page states, responsive behavior, visual tokens, interaction and motion states, assets needed, business model, current local implementation status, and known unknowns.
3. Compare your fresh observations with the attached audits. Mark every item as confirmed, changed, or still unverified. Build a page-by-page checklist; do not claim full coverage based only on top-level links.
4. Present one consolidated implementation plan, suggested project order, repository/file impact, and acceptance checklist to the user. Stop and wait for their review before coding.
Stage 2 — implement after the user approves the plan
- Keep all four sites isolated. Do not blend their design systems, content models, routing or assets.
- Match layout, component hierarchy, responsive behavior, and interaction patterns closely. Use original or licensed copy, imagery, logos, testimonials, and media unless the user confirms rights to reuse exact source material.
- Use the FounderOS public demo source only under its MIT license and preserve its license notice if source code is reused.
- Never carry session tokens, private query parameters, cookies, or personal data into the clone. Forms and CTAs must use local/demo states unless the user provides an authorized destination.
- Implement reusable page templates for repeated lesson, catalog, article, service and industry routes; use route/data registries to keep route coverage auditable.
- Match meaningful motion and states, including hover/focus, menus, accordions, tabs, graph filters/search/detail/fullscreen, sandbox simulations, reduced motion and mobile/touch paths.
- Validate every route and every interactive state in the approved scope at desktop and mobile widths. Record unimplemented pages, unavailable content and differences instead of hiding gaps.
Routing and project handling
The user required that anything sent to Codex go to the Token Works task session. No task URL/ID or destination repository was included when this pack was assembled. Do not push this file or work to another task/session or repository. Keep the work local until the exact Token Works destination is provided.
Existing local references at assembly time:
- Structure Webworks draft Site project: /workspace/sites/structure-webworks-clone (inspect before edits; not published here).
- FounderOS public MIT demo repo: /workspace/scratch/8e1440bc47a0/FounderOS-DEMO (read-only audit; main at ad46d77; clean when checked).
- Current source audit documents are reproduced in the appendices below. The Free System Design/GTM and FounderOS docs are audit briefs, not completed code clones.
- No FSD or GTM clone implementation repository was identified in the workspace.
Project index and current scope
ID	Project	Reference(s)	Known page/system scope	Current evidence/status
A	Structure Webworks	https://structurewebworks.com/ and the supplied AI social-media article	Home, services, five service detail pages, industries, five industry detail pages, work, blog/newsletter archive, editorial article template, contact, legal pages	Detailed audit and Codex prompt in Appendix A; a local Sites draft exists. Supplied article URL was indexed but returned 404 at its clean route; no mcp_token may be retained.
B	Free System Design	https://freesystemdesign.com/	Home, About, Privacy, 46 lesson routes, lesson Learn/Build states, 16 build/play sandboxes, 8 curriculum phases	Page families, lesson inventory and first lesson/build interaction documented in Appendix B. Full recursive route/state capture remains incomplete.
C	GTM AI / Context Graph	https://gtm.ai/	Marketing site, docs, guides, marketplace, catalog, playground, pricing, FAQ, framework, releases, start-building integrations	Homepage and 63 linked path/query variants recorded in Appendix B. Marketplace currently reports 507 catalog entries; route-by-route inspection remains incomplete.
D	FounderOS	https://www.thefounderos.com/; https://github.com/Bennettxai/FounderOS-DEMO	Marketing landing page plus the G-Brain application route /brain interactive graph reference	Graph, brain/vault, directory, panels and source motion mechanics documented in Appendix C. Public repo is MIT; marketing widget and app graph are related but not verified pixel-identical.
E	Extracted AI resources	Two supplied Google Docs	34 unique links across Claude plug-ins/skills/MCP, agent projects, RAG, local AI, etc.	Full categorized link catalog is Appendix D. Descriptions summarize the source documents, not independent technical evaluations.


Cross-project execution sequence
1. Audit all source routes, including menus, footer links, pagination, dynamic route data and query variations; make a route/state ledger per project.
2. Inspect existing local work and identify a non-destructive destination structure inside Token Works.
3. Build each brand in an isolated app/package with its own tokens, shared shell, page templates and content schema.
4. Populate every confirmed route/state from source observations and licensed/user-provided content. Where source copy/media cannot be reused, write original replacements that serve the same content purpose.
5. Implement interaction and motion parity with keyboard, focus, touch and reduced-motion behavior.
6. Verify the route checklist, layout breakpoints, interaction states, links/forms, and console/build health; report exact coverage and remaining differences.
Acceptance standard
- Every verified public route resolves and uses the correct template/content record.
- No dead navigation, placeholder buttons, fake external integrations or form submissions to the reference sites.
- All observed interactive states work and remain accessible; reduced-motion is respected.
- Visual hierarchy, density, spacing, typography, contrast, responsive behavior and graph/simulator behavior are compared against source captures.
- All reused source code/assets have documented licenses; protected third-party wording/media is not copied without rights.
- A final coverage report lists routes and states completed, deviations, unresolved source pages and tests run.
Appendix map
- Appendix A: Structure Webworks site and article audit, business model, design/motion inventory, and Codex-specific implementation prompt.
- Appendix B: Free System Design and GTM AI audit, all currently observed FSD lesson routes, GTM path/query sample, product/business models, and implementation guidance.
- Appendix C: FounderOS marketing page and G-Brain graph audit, source architecture, state transitions and motion timings.
- Appendix D: Complete extracted AI resources catalog from both Google Docs (34 unique resources).

Structure Webworks — Website Audit & Codex Clone Brief
Prepared: 28 September 2026
Reference site: https://structurewebworks.com/
Requested article: https://structurewebworks.com/blog/62-ai-agents-run-your-entire-social-media-team
Purpose: Give Codex a page inventory, design system, motion specification, business-model summary, and implementation brief for a high-fidelity, responsive site recreation.
1. Scope, coverage, and evidence notes
The public site navigation and indexed page content identify these main page families:
- Home
- Services overview and five service detail pages
- Industries overview and five industry detail pages
- Work / case studies
- Newsletters archive and individual editorial posts
- Contact
- Privacy Policy and Terms & Conditions
The sitemap endpoint could not be retrieved during this review. The inventory below is based on the live home-page navigation and footer, visible section content, direct page checks where available, and indexed search results. The article slug supplied by the user is indexed, but its clean URL returned a 404 in the live browser. Treat the article template and content as an indexed reference, not as a live visual inspection. Do not include the mcp_token query string in implementation, logs, examples, or shared links.
This brief captures the site’s confirmed page types, sections, and shared patterns. It does not claim that every one of the archive’s individual posts has been manually opened and visually checked. Codex should crawl and inventory the full archive before declaring the clone complete.
2. Business model brief
Positioning
Structure Webworks presents itself as a senior, end-to-end digital product and growth partner for SaaS companies and operationally complex service businesses, especially in Canada and the US. The central promise is one senior team that can design, build, and grow a product, with delivery proof through weekly demos, fixed quotes, and revenue-linked measurement.
Likely revenue model, based on public pages
1. Fixed-scope digital product projects: web design, web applications, SaaS MVPs/platforms, and industry-specific operating systems. The site emphasizes costed scopes, fixed quotes, defined delivery windows, weekly releases, and client ownership of the delivered system.
2. Industry-specific implementation packages: configured operating layers for automotive, home services, contractors, legal, and financial businesses. These are described as fixed-price builds that connect existing data/workflows and are owned by the client. Public pages describe modules and rollout phases, but no rate card or self-serve subscription checkout was visible.
3. Recurring growth work: SEO/Core Web Vitals, digital marketing, analytics, campaigns, reputation, and ongoing launch-and-care programs. These imply retainers or ongoing engagements; exact terms and prices are not published in the reviewed material.
4. Lead generation through content: the newsletter/blog publishes technical explainers and AI-agent system designs, builds topical authority, and routes readers toward “Book a call” / “Start a project.” The footer also invites email subscriptions.
5. Sales conversion: free 30-minute intro calls, a project inquiry form, published email/phone, client logos, outcome metrics, reviews, and case-study calls to action.
Business-model interpretation and limits
This reads as a productized professional-services model with fixed-price implementation projects and ongoing growth/support revenue, rather than a publicly demonstrated standalone SaaS subscription business. The vertical “platform” language describes client-specific systems and connected modules; do not assume a common multi-tenant product is sold directly without verifying it. Publicly stated performance metrics and AI case examples are marketing claims and should be reproduced as reference content only when the user intentionally wants those claims; do not invent new proof, clients, or figures. Pricing was not published in the reviewed pages.
Funnel
Awareness via SEO/newsletter and industry pages → proof via outcomes, logos, demos, and workflow examples → book a free call or submit a project inquiry → discovery and costed scope → design/build with weekly demos → launch, care, SEO and growth engagements.
3. Page inventory and section map
All pages should share the same header, navigation, CTA behavior, newsletter/footer, and responsive rules unless a specific page type below requires an intentional variation.
Core pages
Route	Page	Confirmed sections / content
/	Home	Header; centered hero with rating badge, headline, subhead, primary and secondary CTAs, proof points; layered product analytics dashboard illustration; integrations/client-tool logo strip; five service cards; four-stage “How we work”; four “Why us” proof cards; customer logos; five industry cards; testimonial/proof area; final CTA; newsletter and full footer.
/services	Services overview	Intro / positioning; five linked service cards; “From brief to launch” process; final CTA; footer.
/industries	Industries overview	Intro focused on booking-led, ops-heavy companies; five industry cards / proof-led entry points; CTA/footer.
/work	Work / case studies	Linked from home hero. Recreate as the portfolio index only after Codex verifies the current live page, card count, filters, and detail routes; do not invent projects.
/contact	Contact	Heading and response promise; inquiry form fields for name, work email, phone, company website, project details; send button; free 30-minute intro call CTA; direct email/phone; final CTA/footer.
/privacy	Privacy Policy	Legal text page linked from newsletter consent and footer. Preserve exact current policy text after crawling.
/terms	Terms & Conditions	Legal text page linked from footer. Preserve exact current terms after crawling.


Service detail pages
Every service page uses the shared hero / credibility-stat / explanation / service-specific sections / process / FAQ or proof / final CTA / footer pattern. Verify actual section order and count when crawling each page.
Route	Service and confirmed content
/services/web-design	“Interfaces that convert”; research-led UX and visual design for landing pages, marketing sites, and product UI; conversion uplift and median timeline stats; process explanation and CTA.
/services/web-apps	“Web apps your team actually enjoys using”; dashboards, portals, internal tools; uptime / operations proof; sections for data model, workflows, speed, integrations, adoption; app types; delivery process; FAQ.
/services/seo	SEO & Core Web Vitals; technical SEO, content structure, site performance, and durable search visibility. Crawl for full section order and FAQ.
/services/saas	“From MVP to multi-tenant, on one codebase”; product strategy, design, architecture, billing, onboarding, analytics; day-one system illustration and MVP scope. Crawl remaining sections.
/services/marketing	“Growth tied to revenue, not vanity metrics”; positioning, campaigns, SEO/GEO, conversion; CAC and organic-traffic proof; revenue-linked measurements. Crawl remaining sections.


Industry detail pages
These pages use a productized vertical landing-page template: industry-specific hero; connected-module / workflow metrics; workflow and role-based interface mockups; module breakdown; implementation/rollout sequence; objections/FAQ; CTA/footer. Capture exact page-specific sections, module lists, counts, labels, and legal/compliance language from the source during the clone audit.
Route	Industry and confirmed emphasis
/industries/automotive	Dealerships: inventory, leads, deals, financing, service, payments; 14 connected modules and 8 pipeline stages; dashboard-led operating system.
/industries/home-services	HVAC, plumbing, electrical: inbound calls/leads, booking, dispatch, job execution, payment, reviews; 16 modules and phased rollout.
/industries/contractors	Builders/remodelers/design-build: connected lead → estimate → proposal → contract → schedule → project → change order → invoice → payment → review → repeat flow; 28 modules and 11 steps; project costing and billing.
/industries/legal	Law firms: intake, matter opening, document creation, deadlines, billing; rules-based routing, automation over existing systems. Capture exact compliance disclaimers.
/industries/financial	Mortgage/lending/advisory: trust, qualification, booking, secure document collection, long-cycle nurture layered over existing LOS/CRM; six modules; no automated financial advice; compliance review before launch.


Newsletter archive and editorial posts
Route pattern	Page and requirements
/blog	Newsletter/archive index: “Notes on building and shipping”; practical SEO, performance, SaaS delivery and operations content; category labels; article cards with title, excerpt, “Read newsletter” link; repeated CTA and footer. Confirm pagination/filter behavior and the complete post list on the live page.
/blog/[slug]	Editorial detail template: category, title, summary/lede, readable long-form article with hierarchical headings, workflow/system illustrations, inline CTA/cross-links, related posts if present, newsletter/final CTA, footer. The supplied article’s indexed text covers a 62-agent social-media operating system, eight departments, twenty modules, human approval guardrails, a central orchestrator, Claude, LangGraph and pgvector, plus a shared versioned Brand OS. Clean URL returned 404 in the live browser, so Codex must resolve the canonical current slug or treat it as unavailable.

Codex must obtain the complete live archive list from visible page links / pagination or current canonical data. Use actual source content and imagery; do not generate fake article text as if it were original.
4. Visual design system
The reference is a dark, high-contrast, premium B2B studio site. It uses a black/near-black canvas, restrained warm orange accents, large modern sans-serif headings, generous vertical spacing, muted gray copy, rounded dark cards, thin low-contrast borders, and interface mockups as product proof.
Tokens to verify and centralize
Values below are visual estimates from the rendered desktop page. Codex should sample the live CSS/assets if available and replace estimates with measured tokens.
Token	Starting estimate / use
--color-bg	#111110 to #141412; primary page background
--color-surface	#22221f / #252521; cards and mock UI panels
--color-surface-raised	#2a2a26; hover/raised panels
--color-border	rgba(255,255,255,.08); card and control outlines
--color-text	#f4f3f0; headings and primary text
--color-muted	#9a9994; body and secondary copy
--color-subtle	#696862; metadata and tertiary labels
--color-accent	warm orange/coral, approximately #c64a2b; primary CTA, active cards, micro accents
--color-accent-dark	approximately #8d321f; accent hover / illustration contrast
--color-light	warm white #f0efea; occasional inverse surfaces and chips
--radius-control	pill / full radius on CTAs and small badges
--radius-card	roughly 18–24px on prominent cards; smaller radii for dashboard widgets
--shadow-soft	diffuse, low-opacity warm shadow / glow; never heavy elevation
--content-max	broad centered desktop container; estimate 1,200–1,300px
--section-space	large desktop vertical rhythm; responsive reductions on tablet/mobile


Typography and composition
- Use a contemporary sans-serif with a clean geometric feel. The logo is a compact wolf-mark + wordmark; preserve it only if the user has rights to the provided asset, otherwise use a neutral placeholder mark.
- Hero headings are large, centered, light-weight, tightly tracked, and split across lines; first line is near-white with a muted-gray phrase / gradient-like emphasis. Section headings are left-aligned or centered according to the section.
- Eyebrows are tiny uppercase labels with letter spacing and orange bullet/dot; metadata is subdued.
- Body copy is small-to-medium, muted, short line length, and relaxed line height.
- CTA hierarchy: solid warm-orange pill for primary action; transparent dark pill with hairline border for secondary; external-link arrow glyphs are used as affordance.
- Most feature sections use spacious dark backgrounds rather than alternating large color bands. Large cards have thin outlines, soft gradients, subtle glows and rounded corners.
- The home service cards form an overlapping vertical stack. Each card combines a custom UI illustration to the left and service name/copy on the right. The active card is saturated orange and foregrounded; inactive cards recede into dark surfaces.
- Product screenshots are represented as bespoke interface mockups: KPI tiles, bars, status chips, tables, calendar/dispatch widgets, badges. Match the actual card content and color tone; avoid generic stock photography.
- Industry cards combine concise business outcomes with mini workflow UI fragments. Client logos sit in muted tonal containers.
- Footer is dense but ordered in columns, with newsletter form, service and industry link groups, company/support/legal links and social icons.

The repo may have nested routes or API endpoints not listed in README. The user's current focus is the public marketing site and interactive knowledge graph, so the /brain route should be implemented/tested as the parity reference without claiming all app routes have been audited.
Architecture and data model from public source
- components/KnowledgeGraph.tsx is the radial graph renderer; uses D3-force, SVG and camera transforms.
- components/GraphDirectory.tsx renders grouped, alphabetized, scrollable rows and collapsed rail.
- components/KnowledgeDetail.tsx supplies entity detail cards.
- components/KnowledgeGraphFullscreen.tsx portals the graph into fullscreen, resizes the directory, manages keyboard navigation and body scroll lock.
- components/BrainGraphView.tsx switches between lazy-loaded Radial and Neural graphs and chips department filters.
- /brain server-loads graph data, memory constellation, wiki details, run states, client roster and board seats; graph view fills available vertical space.
- G-Brain stores Markdown documents, chunks/embeds them, and supports hybrid keyword/semantic retrieval with local grep fallback.
- Optimal Engine governs facts through Source → Signal → Claim → Fact → Memory; facts require review before promotion.
- Demo repo uses seeded placeholder business data; integrations report honest connected, not_configured or error status.
Implementation guardrails and validation
1. Keep marketing site sections and /brain as separate page surfaces. Use the app source for interaction mechanics/data structures, not as evidence that the marketing embed has every app-only control.
2. Build graph affordances accessibly: real buttons/labels, keyboard paths, touch drag/pan fallback and reduced-motion mode.
3. Keep graph and directory state synchronized: hover highlights chain; select opens detail; back closes detail but retains current directory; close clears focus.
4. Verify the graph at normal, note-search, node-detail, directory-collapsed, fullscreen and reduced-motion states, plus narrow viewport.
5. Preserve the public demo's MIT license when reusing repository code. Avoid sending commits upstream; target only the user's Token Works task session once provided.
6. Use original or licensed assets/copy for the new project unless source reuse rights cover the exact material.
